newsitem.title: FINLAND: INGMAN SEES NEGATIVE TREND AFFECTING 97.
newsitem.headline: INGMAN SEES NEGATIVE TREND AFFECTING 97.

text.p: Finnish dairy group Ingman Foods Oy Ab said on Friday that negative developments in its operating environment would have a significant impact on its 1997 earnings.
"There has recently occurred a negative trend in the company's operating environment that will have a significant effect on earnings in 1997," Ingman said in a statement.
Ingman said the negative trend was due to the rising average price it had to pay for milk, which it said it could not fully shift into product prices.
"In comparison with the 1995 average price level ... the 1997 price level for milk raw material will rise five to ten penni per litre," Ingman said.
In January-August, Ingman swung to a 8.4 million markka profit after financial items from a 7.7 million markka loss in the year-ago period. Its full-1995 result was a 1.9 million markka loss.
In October, Ingman said it expected to make a slight loss in the final part of the year, but that the full-year would show a slight profit.
"The restoration of the profitability of the dairy products division is taking place more slowly than forecast," the company said in its Friday statement.
Ingman said cheese prices had not risen in line with expectations, and that it had not made as many production subcontracts for ice cream exports as before.
